chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the junub: may he eat, drink, and recite the Qur'an? He said: Yes, he may eat, drink, recite the Qur'an, and remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as much as he wishes.

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.يَأْكُلُ: he eats; permission to consume food
key_terms.يَشْرَبُ: he drinks; permission to consume drink

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah eat, drink, and recite the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a person in the state of janabah may eat, drink, recite the Qur'an, and engage in dhikr of Allah عزّ وجلّ. It conveys a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and clarifies that these acts are permitted for the junub.
